# Unwrapped positioned pictures across hard breaks

Four original OPC/XML controls are generated by
`tools/positioned_breaks_fixture.py` using Python's standard library. The panel
PNG is original repository fixture artwork. Each contains healthy heading and
ending text plus two wrapNone pictures, one before and one after a page/column
break within the same paragraph. Vertical bases are paragraph and line; the
column cases use two section columns. No corpus artwork or fonts are copied.

The previous implementation imported rich structure but rejected its layout,
even in best-effort mode. Opening therefore discarded positioned pictures and
explicit pagination in a one-page plain-text approximation. The current layout
keeps each unwrapped drawing in its hard-break segment. Paragraph-relative
coordinates restart at the segment's first line; line-relative coordinates
continue to use the drawing's own line. Page cases retain two pages and column
cases retain both columns on one page. Ordinary line breaks retain their existing
paragraph-relative origin. Wrapped drawings across hard breaks remain guarded.

Fresh native metadata is bound to each source hash in `*-native.json`.
`tools/record-positioned-breaks-metadata.ps1` records an already-open exact source
without saving it, reading font programs, exporting PDF, or closing the reference application.
Picture origins in these controls derive from their column and paragraph/line
anchor origins plus numeric offsets. Range.Information caret positions have
screen-pixel precision: comparisons use a 0.75pt bound for vertical origins,
exact horizontal origins and exact dimensions. This is not a glyph-ink or PDF
baseline reference. The original optional PDF assertions remain unchanged.
The column/line control was also compared visually with the native reference.

Five unit checks cover both layout modes, drawing placement, source preservation
and the wrapped-content guard. Eight browser cases cover native metadata,
printing both retained pictures, no-edit package preservation, text insertion,
export/reopen, unrelated-part preservation, exact undo and redo. Other anchor,
wrapping and following-paragraph controls provide separate regressions.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses are 17.3.3.1 (br), 20.4.2.3 (anchor),
20.4.2.11 (positionV), 20.4.2.15 (wrapNone), and 20.4.3.5 (ST_RelFromV).
The combination is valid markup; no specification/native divergence is claimed.

A fresh streaming XML scan of all 368 non-lock corpus packages, including both
large XML sources, found no paragraph containing both wp:anchor and a page/column
w:br in the selected document/header/footer parts. This general missing-feature
fix does not resolve or promote a current corpus template.
